children: Zacks Investment Research has recently initiated coverage of
Interlink Electronics, Inc.

LINK with a Neutral recommendation. The research report highlights the sensor technology company’s improving profitability, expanding revenue base and acquisition-driven growth opportunities, while noting customer concentration, industrial-market weakness and mixed valuation as factors that warrant a balanced investment view.

Interlink, headquartered in Fremont, CA, provides advanced sensing technologies and printed electronics solutions used across medical, industrial, automotive, consumer electronics, wearables and environmental-monitoring applications.

Interlink’s recent results reflect improving operating performance. Second-quarter 2026 revenues increased 10.4% year over year to $3.8 million, while operating income rose to $0.3 million from $0.07 million. For the first half of 2026, gross profit increased 20.9% and the net loss narrowed to $0.1 million from $0.7 million. Medical and standard-product revenues advanced 30.5% and 34.8%, respectively, during the first six months, broadening the company’s revenue base and reducing its reliance on weaker industrial demand.

Acquisitions, cross-selling opportunities and long-lived design wins provide additional growth avenues, as highlighted by the research report. Interlink has expanded into gas sensing, printed electronics, membrane keypads and smart-textile technologies through acquisitions, while acquired businesses have improved gross margins following integration. The company is also pursuing a strategic acquisition announced in May 2026 that it expects to complete by the end of October.

Long-lived design wins and exposure to growing sensing markets further support the company’s prospects. Successful engineering projects can transition into multi-year production programs, while some Interlink products have remained active for more than 20 years. Its exposure to medical, environmental, industrial, wearable and automotive applications also positions the company to participate in demand across several expanding sensing markets.

However, customer concentration and weakness in industrial markets remain notable headwinds, as outlined in the report. Two customers represented about 30% of second-quarter 2026 revenues, making results more sensitive to changes in order timing or demand from major accounts. Industrial revenues declined 25.8% year over year in the second quarter and 18.8% during the first half, reflecting reduced shipments and softer demand for gas-sensing products.

Margin sustainability, spending trends and valuation also warrant attention. Although first-half gross margin improved, second-quarter gross margin slipped to 44.4% from 45% because of product and customer mix, while SG&A expenses continued to increase. Lower R&D spending could also constrain organic innovation if the decline reflects reduced development capacity rather than efficiencies.

Interlink’s shares have delivered strong recent performance, signaling increased investor interest in the company’s growth prospects. From a valuation perspective, however, the picture is mixed. The stock appears relatively more attractive on a sales-based measure compared with industry and sector benchmarks, while its book-value-based valuation carries a premium.

Overall, improving profitability, strength in medical and standard products, acquisition-led expansion and long-lived design wins support Interlink’s growth prospects, while customer concentration, industrial weakness, margin sensitivity and spending-related risks temper the outlook, supporting a balanced stance on the shares.
